questions.q: What is OpenZeppelin, as described in this lesson?
options: A Remix-specific plugin with no real code in it
A blockchain competing with Ethereum
A real library of audited, pre-written, vetted Solidity building blocks
A Solidity compiler version
questions.explain: OpenZeppelin provides audited building blocks for Solidity code — contracts that are already safe, efficient, and vetted by other developers.

questions.q: What is the real, key difference between a library and a contract in Solidity?
options: Contracts can only have pure functions; libraries can have any kind
There is no real difference between them
Libraries can't hold state variables or support inheritance; contracts can do both
Libraries can send and receive Ether, but contracts cannot
questions.explain: Libraries are stateless and don't support inheritance — contracts can hold state and support inheritance, among other differences.

questions.q: What does `using MathLib for uint;` actually let you do?
options: Automatically convert every uint into a string
Delete the MathLib library after one use
Call MathLib's functions directly on a uint value, like val.double()
Give every uint variable a starting value of zero
questions.explain: The using keyword attaches a library's functions to a type, so you can call them with dot syntax directly on a value of that type.

questions.q: What's the real, practical difference between an embedded and a deployed library?
options: There is no real cost difference between the two
Deployed libraries are always cheaper than embedded ones
Embedded (internal-only) libraries get copied into your contract at compile time; deployed libraries (with public/external functions) are deployed and linked separately, at more gas cost
Embedded libraries can never be reused across contracts
questions.explain: Keeping library functions internal lets Solidity embed the code directly at compile time (cheaper); public/external functions require separate deployment and linking (more expensive).

questions.q: What real, practical way did the instructor demonstrate for importing a file directly from GitHub?
options: It's not actually possible to import directly from GitHub
Only OpenZeppelin's paid tier supports GitHub imports
Downloading the file manually and re-uploading it to Remix
Pasting the file's raw GitHub URL directly inside the import statement's quotes
questions.explain: The instructor imported OpenZeppelin's strings.sol directly by pasting its GitHub URL inside the import statement — no manual copy-paste of the file's contents required.
